agree.reason: The page is clear and believable, but an owner who pays her cousin $600 a year will see $199 a month (about $2,400 a year) and find nothing that explains why it's worth four times as much, so she probably won't book.

honest.reason: Most claims match the brief, but 'clients who'd been with me for years' is invented, 'One owner saved $800' turns what a client said into a fact, and 'You won't get a low starting rate that jumps later' is a promise the January price rise already undercuts.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are repeated as given rather than worked out: it never says no client left for any reason other than selling, that roughly 3 in 10 clients got a lower accountant bill, that the deadline was met 9 of 12 months, or how the $800 saving compares with the yearly price.

right_comparison.reason: The page never describes the reader's real alternative, which is books done once a year at tax time with no monthly close, payroll or sales tax filing, so the $199 is never set against what she has now.

qualification.reason: The missed deadline and the Sunday–Monday phone hours are stated plainly with numbers, but the page doesn't say what a late close means for the client or what happens when one occurs.

objections.reason: The page answers objections about firm size and price fairness, but not the obvious one for this reader: why pay monthly when tax-time help costs $600 a year, even though the $800 saving and the monthly payroll and sales tax work could have answered it.

fit.reason: It is about 330 words of sales-page text, scannable, and ends with a booking button as the brief asked.
